visualReview.notes: Inspected53 current frames:12 portable,12 shared-material/flat-map and29 Earth-rig/tier views. Six-lane roadway, pale four-plate-girder river unit, broad transverse concrete piers, longer land approaches, lower separate paths, west bank bends, east path loop, rails, median and slender paired-arm lights remain coherent. Source retains dense railing pickets; browser tiers aggregate them and far tiers omit furniture. Main girder unit is423m, not stretched to the866m mapped full viaduct. Signed lower-path ramps follow the standard PMTiles extract. Three shared concrete/coated-metal/aggregate graphs use metric UVs; palette paint and no private images. Default whole-crossing/context views are too distant for fine detail; authored road/path/underside cameras provide that inspection. Flat synthetic ground does not prove native bank contact; coarse terrain samples and the PMTiles plan supply the approximate fit. Some High shadow maps show repeated thin-geometry shadow aliasing on the long road/girder; portable geometry and deck ray checks show no missing panels. Reconstructed pier/approach spacing, unsurveyed water datum, ramp grades/contacts, representative service pipes and unmeasured physical-device performance remain explicit.

runtimeLodReview.notes: Four authored browser tiers with at most four draws, separate position/normal streams and no private/embedded images. Detailed source master remains separate. Physical laptop/phone and dense-city timings are not measured.

windingRepair.repair: Every loft in lazienkowski-model.mjs was inside-out: the deck slabs (concrete), the 3.5 cm wearing course, the four steel girder webs and flanges, the four river piers and the three lower cycle-path slabs listed each section ring bottom-first (or clockwise from above), the opposite of the order authored-structure-mesh loft() winds outward, so every face pointed into its solid and the near side was culled (14.9% of the model saw through, 72% of the deck concrete). A loftOut() helper now reverses each ring before lofting, so the same faces wind and face outward; vertex positions and materials are unchanged (vertex multiset, triangle counts and per-material areas identical; scan 0.00% on source and all four LODs). Recaptured frames show the deck edges, road and path decks solid, without the transverse segment seams and see-through soffit boxes of the old frames; the deck sides and piers now take sun and shadow on their outward faces. The pre-existing diagonal shadow banding on the road and girder webs in medium-fi high frames is unchanged.
windingRepair.evidence: Inside-out faces found by a software depth-raster see-through scan of every runtime GLB (back faces of single-sided opaque materials nearest the viewer from above-horizon views). Same polygons with corrected facing; a non-planar quad may split along its other diagonal. Rescan of source and all four runtime LODs is clean. Portable, shared-surface and medium-fi frames were recaptured from the repaired model and inspected; the existing review statuses and notes are retained. Still bound to the previous model: runtimeLodReview level hashes describe the previous runtime LODs (the medium-fi recapture covers the repaired ones).
